purpose: Restore Soviet-period OCR in Digi using Platforma Digitizare, with an advanced document handoff and confirmed saving into the originating user's drafts.

components.startup: scripts/start_server.py starts the worker alongside the existing Django service

behavior: New Digi uploads no longer fan out into the ten historical remote OCR folders. Processing starts explicitly from the media manager.
Simple jobs use the existing Soviet XX FineReader Hot Folder output and period 0 transliteration.
Jobs and completed file results persist in SQLite; the worker resumes unfinished jobs after restart.
The advanced link carries a job-scoped capability in a URL fragment. The frontend removes it from history and keeps progress in sessionStorage for refresh recovery.
Standalone Platforma Digitizare users can connect a Digi account from the final step before saving.
Draft ownership is derived from the authenticated Digi session that created the job, never from a browser-supplied user ID.
Saving returns the confirmed draft ID and an owned-draft editor link. Retries reuse the same draft; corrected content updates it.
PDF sources receive download links. OCR with no recognized text returns an error.
Historical inputs and outputs were preserved. Hot Folder inputs were subsequently separated by period; see hotfolder-windows-2026-11-18.json.

configuration.credential_policy: The service key stays in private runtime configuration; browser handoffs use separate scoped capabilities.
configuration.simple_image_input: Prepared in backend/media/pre/OpenCV/prepared/secolulXX; actual cache misses are staged with fresh names into backend/media/pre/OpenCV/secolulXX.

deployment.php_note: PHP 8.2 CLI is incompatible with the installed Carbon version; PHP 7.4 fails Composer requirements. PHP 8.1 was verified.
deployment.flarum_build: cd integrations/digi-media-manager/js && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run build
deployment.rollback: Restore the backed-up extension files and frontend assets, restore the previous backend code, then restart Django. Preserve job tables, documents and runtime records; a database rollback is not required to restore the prior interface.

verification.legacy_test_runner_limitations: The pre-existing npm test task stops at legacy StepZilla lint, and tests/main.spec.js imports a missing legacy module. Application tests were run directly with Mocha, excluding that legacy file.
verification.flarum_checks: PHP syntax passed; ownership, duplicate avoidance, corrected-draft updates and empty-result rejection passed using synthetic records rolled back after verification
verification.simple_real_pipeline: New synthetic JPG with spaces and diacritics plus a PDF: upload, OCR, transliteration, draft creation and duplicate retry succeeded in about 85 seconds
verification.advanced_browser: Import, capability removal, refresh recovery, OpenCV and OCR succeeded. The automation did not navigate to the transliteration button; no page errors were reported.
verification.advanced_completion: The already-completed OCR output was transliterated and saved through the real scoped callback with HTTP 200, without repeating OCR
verification.test_documents: Two private drafts labelled TEST were preserved; no public article was published
verification.additional_testing: Stopped further testing at the user's request

operational_limits: The Windows machine, Django worker and FineReader Hot Folder must remain available; startup follows the existing user-login service arrangement.
FineReader still uses Hot Folder rather than Extended CLI export.
OpenCV images now enter one period-specific inbox. Changing the selected period after preprocessing can intentionally stage that image to another model.
